identityRebind.scope: mGBA gbAs ROM identity bytes $04..$1f only
identityRebind.gameplayPayload: byte-identical to bootstrap outside identity bytes

determinism.statement: two independent runs of every comparable mapped tick produced byte-identical PNGs (full set, not a sample)

contract.note: ROM reference is the native 160x144 framebuffer; its battle world is rows 24..103 (80 rows, ACTION_NATIVE_H). The remake output is 320x180 with the ROM world 320x160 centred at output y=10 (BATTLE_OUTPUT_Y). Comparison downscales the remake world crop x0.5 to 160x80 and quantises both sides to GBC 5-bit colour, which removes the 5-bit->8-bit expansion convention difference (ROM PNGs use round(v*255/31); the remake uses v<<3).

tickMapping.kind: romFrame -> remake presentation tick (piecewise 1:1 GBC-frame offset table)
tickMapping.note: The ROM frame counter (savestate-relative) and the remake BattleRuntime GBC tick share no clock. Each segment anchors a ROM phase on the beat the remake declares for the same phase and advances 1:1 because both sides count GBC frames. Frames whose phase has NO_REMAKE_BEAT are still captured and are expected to diverge — that divergence is the measurement, not an artifact.
